questions.question: How many kūpuna in my district rely on Social Security as their primary income?
questions.universe: People 65+; define individual versus household income and “primary” (e.g. >50%) before measurement.
questions.required_indicators: Joint age × Social Security receipt × share of total income.
questions.already_available: No exact count. Raw DP03 rows 74–77 report all-household Social Security/retirement receipt and recipient-household means.
questions.additional_source: S0103 adds households with older householders receiving Social Security; B19037 adds older-householder income. Neither measures primary dependence. PUMS only for a separately defined state/PUMA study.
questions.geographic_availability: Receipt proxy: direct SLD. Primary-dependence custom estimate: state/PUMA only.
questions.answerability: Exact district answer unsupported; offer clearly labeled receipt proxy, not dependence.
questions.methodological_limits: Social Security ≠ SSI; receipt ≠ reliance; household benefit total ≠ person count. No multiplication of marginal totals.

questions.question: What percentage of residents in my district are 65 or older?
questions.universe: All residents.
questions.required_indicators: Age 65+ share and MOE.
questions.already_available: Mapped older_adult_share; raw DP05 row 27 percentage.
questions.additional_source: None.
questions.answerability: Reported estimate available now.
questions.methodological_limits: Use published percent/MOE; retain total-population universe and 2020–2024 period.

questions.question: How many kūpuna in my district live below the poverty line?
questions.universe: People 65+ for whom poverty status is determined.
questions.required_indicators: Age 65+ below-poverty count and matched denominator.
questions.already_available: Raw DP03 row 145 has 65+ poverty rate/MOE, but its count is (X).
questions.additional_source: B17001; S0103 as a complementary profile.
questions.answerability: Count is a documented sum of disjoint age/sex poverty cells after import; existing rate can be exposed now.
questions.methodological_limits: Do not multiply DP05 total 65+ population by the DP03 poverty rate; poverty excludes some residents.

questions.question: Are older residents in my district more likely to rent or own their homes?
questions.universe: Literal: people 65+ in occupied housing. Available alternative: households with householder 65+.
questions.required_indicators: Age × tenure with person or household universe made explicit.
questions.already_available: No age × tenure cross-tab in current profiles.
questions.additional_source: B25007; B25011 for older people living alone by tenure.
questions.geographic_availability: Direct SLD for older-householder household measure.
questions.answerability: Answer reworded household measure after import; literal all-older-residents measure not established by these tables.
questions.methodological_limits: A 65+ householder is not every 65+ resident. Do not relabel household tenure as resident tenure.

questions.question: How does the kūpuna population in my district compare with the statewide average?
questions.universe: All residents, identifying age cutoff 65+.
questions.required_indicators: Age 65+ count/share for district and state.
questions.already_available: Mapped age_65_plus and older_adult_share in both geographies.
questions.additional_source: None.
questions.answerability: Reported estimates and calculated percentage-point difference available.
questions.methodological_limits: Statewide share is not an average district count; district is part of state, so uncertainty is correlated.

questions.question: How many older adults live alone in my district?
questions.universe: People 65+ living in one-person households; excludes group quarters.
questions.required_indicators: Older male-alone + older female-alone counts.
questions.already_available: Raw DP02 rows 12 and 16, each with MOE; not in chatbot allowlist.
questions.additional_source: None for total; B09021 for richer arrangements or B25011 for tenure.
questions.answerability: Derived disjoint-cell sum using existing data; expose controlled formula/MOE.
questions.methodological_limits: Count people/one-person households consistently; do not include institutional residence or infer loneliness.

questions.question: How many families in my district struggle to afford basic necessities?
questions.universe: Families of a defined composition; hardship needs an operational definition.
questions.required_indicators: Family composition-specific budget threshold jointly with comparable disposable/gross income and costs.
questions.already_available: Poverty rates, income bands and housing burden are available proxies; no direct hardship count.
questions.additional_source: DBEDT 2024 Self-Sufficiency Income Standard; B19037/B17024 give limited additional context.
questions.geographic_availability: Budget: county/state, not SLD. Income/poverty proxies: direct SLD.
questions.answerability: Can report measured proxies and county budget scenarios; exact family hardship count unsupported.
questions.methodological_limits: Family ≠ household; basic-needs budgets ≠ Census poverty. A broad income band cannot determine how many families fall below a composition-specific threshold.

questions.question: What percentage of households spend more than 30% of their income on housing?
questions.universe: Occupied households with computable housing-cost share, split renter, owner with mortgage, owner without mortgage.
questions.required_indicators: 30–34.9 and 35%+ cells plus each computed-universe denominator.
questions.already_available: DP04 raw rows 127/131/132,134/140/141,155/160/161. Most counts mapped; unmortgaged denominator only raw.
questions.additional_source: None for ≥30% computed-universe estimate; B25106 adds income cross-tabs.
questions.answerability: Derived weighted count/denominator ratio after raw retrieval; not average of three percentages.
questions.methodological_limits: Bins support ≥30%, not strict >30%. Exclude and disclose not-computed cases; use appropriate derived MOE.

questions.question: How many households in my district earn less than $50,000 annually?
questions.universe: Households; annual household income in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars.
questions.required_indicators: Sum the five income bins below $50,000.
questions.already_available: Mapped income_profile_01–05 / DP03 rows 60–64.
questions.additional_source: None; B19037 only if age subgroup requested.
questions.answerability: Derived sum available from existing records; current tool returns brackets, not a guaranteed summed fact.
questions.methodological_limits: Households do not necessarily earn wages; income includes other sources. Propagate MOE; sum estimates, not margins of error.

questions.question: Are residents in my district experiencing higher poverty rates than neighboring districts?
questions.universe: People with poverty status determined, same chamber/period; define spatial neighbor.
questions.required_indicators: Poverty rates/MOEs plus shared-boundary adjacency from existing polygons.
questions.already_available: Mapped poverty_rate for all districts; existing PostGIS geometry sufficient for adjacency.
questions.additional_source: None for rates; B17001 adds actual poverty counts/denominators.
questions.answerability: Descriptive comparison now for named districts; spatial-neighbor tool and significance method still needed.
questions.methodological_limits: Numerically consecutive districts need not be neighbors. Rook versus point-touch adjacency must be stated; “higher estimate” does not imply significant difference.

questions.question: How does median household income compare with median rent in my district?
questions.universe: All households for income; renter-occupied units paying cash rent for median gross rent.
questions.required_indicators: Annual median household income and monthly median gross rent.
questions.already_available: Both mapped, with MOEs.
questions.additional_source: None.
questions.answerability: Display both now; optional annualized rent/income benchmark as a clearly labeled ratio of separate medians.
questions.methodological_limits: Different universes. 12×median rent / median income is not the median household’s burden or the share of renters cost-burdened.

questions.question: How many households rely on government assistance as a source of income?
questions.universe: Households; define specific benefit and whether receipt or dependence is intended.
questions.required_indicators: SSI, cash public assistance, SNAP and possibly a published union; primary-income share would be separate.
questions.already_available: Raw DP03 78/80/82 gives separate SSI/cash/SNAP receipt counts, not reliance or union.
questions.additional_source: B19058 provides cash assistance OR SNAP; S2201 receipt subgroups.
questions.geographic_availability: Direct SLD/county/state for survey receipt; administrative district counts not verified.
questions.answerability: Program-specific receipt answer via raw data; defined union after import; all-assistance dependence count unsupported.
questions.methodological_limits: SNAP is noncash; benefits overlap. Do not add SSI, SNAP and cash counts or infer primary dependence.

questions.question: How many renters in my district are considered severely cost-burdened?
questions.universe: Cash-rent renter-occupied housing units/households with computable share; not individual renters.
questions.required_indicators: Published 50%+ gross-rent/income cell and MOE.
questions.already_available: No. DP04 ends at 35%+; this cannot isolate 50%+.
questions.answerability: Reported 50%+ bin after import, with universe and not-computed exclusions.
questions.methodological_limits: Confirm convention: published ≥50% bin cannot identify strict >50%. Explain household versus person count.

questions.question: What percentage of residents in my district live in owner-occupied housing?
questions.universe: People in occupied housing units, or all residents if explicitly including group quarters in denominator.
questions.required_indicators: Person counts by tenure and appropriate population denominator.
questions.already_available: DP04 owner/renter counts and percentages are households, not people.
questions.additional_source: B25008, with DP05 total population only if all-resident denominator is requested.
questions.answerability: Derived person-based share after import.
questions.methodological_limits: Do not use owner-household share or rounded average household size to manufacture exact resident counts; group quarters alter denominator.

questions.question: Are housing costs higher in my district than in the rest of Honolulu County?
questions.universe: Comparable renter/owner housing universes. “Rest” excludes district and differs from whole county.
questions.required_indicators: Same cost indicator for district and comparator; remainder medians require microdistribution, not subtraction.
questions.already_available: Mapped district and whole-Honolulu medians plus some burden counts.
questions.additional_source: No download for whole-county comparison; full-county/remainder counts may be constructed only for additive compatible cells and containment.
questions.geographic_availability: SLD and whole county directly; county-minus-district median not published in current data.
questions.answerability: Whole-county descriptive benchmark available; exact rest-of-county median unavailable.
questions.methodological_limits: Do not subtract medians. District may not be fully within Honolulu; for multi-county districts provide all relevant county contexts, not a fabricated blended county.

questions.question: How many households might be at risk of housing instability?
questions.universe: Households; requires a validated risk definition and observation period.
questions.required_indicators: Burden, low income, overcrowding, tenure and possibly arrears/eviction/displacement information.
questions.already_available: Several burden, crowding and income proxies in raw DP04/DP03; no instability label or validated risk score.
questions.additional_source: B25070/B25106; HUD CHAS later for housing problems. Administrative eviction/arrears district series not verified.
questions.geographic_availability: Proxy ACS direct SLD; CHAS smaller-area/county; risk outcome coverage unknown.
questions.answerability: Report separately measured risk factors; no defensible unique at-risk count by summing overlaps.
questions.methodological_limits: Cost burden is not a prediction of eviction/homelessness. Adding overlapping vulnerable groups double-counts households.

questions.question: What are the biggest housing-related challenges shown by my district’s demographic data?
questions.universe: Distinct housing/household universes per measure.
questions.required_indicators: Rent, burden, tenure, vacancy, crowding and county/state benchmarks, each with MOE.
questions.already_available: Mapped rent/tenure/burden plus raw DP04 crowding, housing age, value and costs.
questions.additional_source: B25070/B25106 deepen analysis; HHFDC inventory supports referrals, not resident outcomes.
questions.geographic_availability: Direct SLD for ACS; property points for inventory.
questions.answerability: Evidence-based descriptive summary now, with expanded raw retrieval; rank only compatible metrics.
questions.methodological_limits: No causal diagnosis or resident-level inference. Vacancy categories are not necessarily available housing; unequal denominators cannot be combined into one count.

questions.question: Are there more renters or homeowners in my district?
questions.universe: Clarify households versus people; default tenure of occupied households.
questions.required_indicators: Owner/renter occupied household counts.
questions.already_available: Mapped owner_occupied and renter_occupied; DP04 54/55.
questions.additional_source: None for households; B25008 for people.
questions.answerability: Reported household estimates now.
questions.methodological_limits: Call them renter/owner households, not number of property owners or individual renters; a landlord can live elsewhere.

questions.question: How many children under 18 live in my district?
questions.universe: All residents under age 18.
questions.required_indicators: Under-18 population.
questions.already_available: Mapped age_under_18; raw DP05 row 22.
questions.additional_source: None.
questions.answerability: Reported estimate now.
questions.methodological_limits: Use exact under-18 total; do not include the entire 15–19 age-distribution bin.

questions.question: What percentage of households have children under 18?
questions.universe: Households with one or more people under 18, unless own-child relationship is specifically requested.
questions.required_indicators: Published households-with-under18 percent and MOE.
questions.already_available: Raw DP02 row 17, not chatbot allowlist.
questions.additional_source: None.
questions.answerability: Reported percentage once raw retrieval exposed.
questions.methodological_limits: “Children of householder” is narrower than any resident under18; use the requested definition, not sum of household-type subrows.

questions.question: How many children live in households below the poverty line?
questions.universe: Children under18 for whom poverty status is determined; poverty assigned using Census family/unrelated-person rules.
questions.required_indicators: Under18 below-poverty count; clarify family-poverty concept rather than generic household-income cutoff.
questions.already_available: Raw DP03 row 139 provides child-poverty rate only; count (X).
questions.answerability: Disjoint age/sex cell sum after import; rate can be exposed now.
questions.methodological_limits: Household income and family poverty differ. Do not multiply all children by a mismatched rate denominator.

questions.question: What percentage of adults have a bachelor’s degree or higher?
questions.universe: Conventionally population age25+; “adults”18+ is a different question.
questions.required_indicators: Published BA+ percent and MOE for age25+.
questions.already_available: Raw DP02 row 78, denominator row69; not allowlisted.
questions.additional_source: None for25+; an age-specific education table would need separate verification for an18+ request.
questions.answerability: Reported25+ estimate once raw retrieval exposed.
questions.methodological_limits: State age25+ explicitly. BA+ row already includes graduate degrees; do not double-count by adding both a combined total and component.

questions.question: How many grandparents are responsible for raising their grandchildren?
questions.universe: Grandparents living with own grandchildren under18 who report responsibility for basic needs.
questions.required_indicators: Responsible-grandparent people and MOE.
questions.already_available: Raw DP02 row52 (row58 repeats same total in a later section).
questions.additional_source: None for total; S1002 for subgroup detail.
questions.answerability: Reported count once raw retrieval exposed.
questions.methodological_limits: Not necessarily sole/legal custody. Do not double-count repeated total; B10002 counts grandchildren, not grandparents.

questions.question: How does educational attainment in my district compare with the statewide average?
questions.universe: Population25+ in district and state.
questions.required_indicators: Same education category percentages/denominators/MOEs.
questions.already_available: Raw DP02 rows69–78 across all82 geographies.
questions.additional_source: None.
questions.answerability: Reported estimates and calculated percentage-point differences after raw retrieval.
questions.methodological_limits: Compare consistent categories and period; state includes district; differences need appropriate uncertainty handling.

questions.question: Which government assistance programs might be relevant to low-income kūpuna in my district?
questions.universe: District older-adult need signals; program eligibility assessed for individuals/assistance units separately.
questions.required_indicators: Age, poverty, disability, tenure and program-specific rules/referral geography.
questions.already_available: Older share mapped; older poverty/disability/alone and SSI/SS receipt raw. No verified program directory currently imported.
questions.additional_source: Versioned SSI, AABD, SNAP, Med-QUEST, Medicare Savings/Extra Help, housing, H-HEAP and aging-service official records; B17001/S0103 enrich need.
questions.geographic_availability: Need direct SLD; program rules statewide/federal/county service areas; not district eligibility counts.
questions.answerability: Explain potential relevance with citations; individual eligibility requires additional inputs and agency determination.
questions.methodological_limits: 65+ and60+ program cutoffs differ. Low income alone does not establish assets, functional need, status, household unit or availability.

questions.question: How many residents might benefit from affordable housing assistance?
questions.universe: People versus households must be resolved; measured housing need ≠ qualifying applicants.
questions.required_indicators: Burden/AMI-income/tenure/household-size joint cells plus program rules, capacity and actual participation.
questions.already_available: Rent, income and burden proxies only.
questions.additional_source: B25070/B25106, HUD income limits; HUD CHAS later; HPHA/county participation data if published or supplied.
questions.geographic_availability: Direct ACS SLD proxy; HUD county/other areas; district administrative counts not verified.
questions.answerability: Quantify specific measured household needs; no exact eligible-person or unmet-service count.
questions.methodological_limits: Do not subtract county participation from district ACS needs. AMI-adjusted limits differ from a fixed $50k threshold; waitlists and eligibility differ.

questions.question: What demographic indicators suggest a need for food assistance programs?
questions.universe: People in poverty, older people/children, and households reporting SNAP; separate universes.
questions.required_indicators: Poverty and child/older poverty, low income, disability, SNAP receipt, vehicles and food-access context.
questions.already_available: Poverty/income mapped; SNAP, age poverty rates, disability and vehicles raw.
questions.additional_source: B17001/S2201/B22003; program directory.
questions.geographic_availability: ACS direct SLD; administrative participation generally larger reporting areas.
questions.answerability: Report indicators and potential relevance, not a measured food-insecurity count.
questions.methodological_limits: Poverty and SNAP receipt are not direct food insecurity measures; SNAP nonreceipt is not proof of noneligibility or unmet eligible need.

questions.question: Which existing programs support older adults with limited retirement income?
questions.universe: Individuals/assistance units with program-specific ages/resources/Medicare or functional status.
questions.required_indicators: Verified purposes, eligibility rules, benefit types and application/referral paths.
questions.already_available: No program directory in imported sources. Raw retirement/SSI/SS measures offer district context only.
questions.additional_source: Official SSI, AABD, SNAP, Med-QUEST, Medicare Savings, Extra Help, aging/nutrition/Kūpuna Care, housing and H-HEAP records.
questions.geographic_availability: Rules federal/state; county/local administration and availability.
questions.answerability: Program information answer after directory curation, with eligibility caveats.
questions.methodological_limits: Retirement income ≠ total countable income; Social Security retirement is not means-tested SSI. Never promise enrollment or benefits.

questions.question: What information would be needed to estimate how many households might qualify for SNAP?
questions.universe: SNAP assistance units (food purchase/preparation groups), which may differ from ACS households.
questions.required_indicators: Current Hawaiʻi gross/net income rules, deductions, resources where applicable, elderly/disability exceptions, assistance-unit composition, status and other current requirements.
questions.already_available: ACS income bands, household characteristics, reported SNAP receipt; not complete eligibility inputs or joint distribution.
questions.additional_source: Current DHS SNAP rules plus S2201/B22003; validated state/PUMA microsimulation only if later justified.
questions.geographic_availability: Rules statewide; descriptive SLD cells; eligibility simulation not reliable at SLD from marginals.
questions.answerability: Can explain missing inputs; cannot count eligible district households from current aggregates.
questions.methodological_limits: Do not use a contiguous-U.S. income chart, old effective year, poverty threshold as guideline, or all households under a chosen income band as eligible.

questions.question: What demographic trends could help government agencies plan community services?
questions.universe: Consistent resident/household populations across comparable time periods and boundaries.
questions.required_indicators: Age, poverty, disability, income, housing, language and access series with identical definitions/geography.
questions.already_available: One imported2020–2024 period: supports needs snapshot, not change over time.
questions.additional_source: Consistent-vintage prior ACS/Decennial series after boundary review; county/state PEP/LAUS, DOE and service locations for context.
questions.geographic_availability: Direct SLD only for compatible plans; county/state trends separately. 2024 Comparison Profiles omit SLD.
questions.answerability: Snapshot now; documented trend comparisons later.
questions.methodological_limits: Do not join pre/post2022 district numbers as identical areas. Overlapping five-year estimates are correlated; location of a school is not residence of its pupils.
